subtitle: Monthly horror picks for the mortally curious.

novels.title: Rebecca
novels.author: Daphne du Maurier (1938)
novels.vibe: The classic gothic romance-thriller about a new bride haunted by the shadow of her husband's dead first wife — and the great house that seems to still belong to her.
novels.summary: A shy young woman marries the wealthy widower Maxim de Winter and moves into his grand estate, Manderley, only to find herself living in the constant shadow of his glamorous first wife, Rebecca. As the sinister housekeeper Mrs. Danvers keeps Rebecca's memory alive, the new Mrs. de Winter uncovers dark secrets behind Rebecca's death.
novels.warnings: Death, psychological manipulation and gaslighting, domestic abuse themes, suicide (referenced), fire.

novels.title: The Turn of the Screw
novels.author: Henry James (1898)
novels.vibe: The ambiguous, endlessly-debated ghost story of a governess convinced malevolent spirits are stalking the children in her care at a remote English estate.
novels.summary: A young governess takes a position at an isolated country house, caring for two children who seem increasingly under the influence of the ghosts of two former servants. As she becomes convinced the children are in supernatural danger, the story leaves deliberately unclear whether the haunting is real or a symptom of her own unraveling.
novels.warnings: Death of children (implied/ambiguous), psychological horror, child endangerment, ambiguous supernatural threat.

novels.title: Mexican Gothic
novels.author: Silvia Moreno-Garcia (2020)
novels.vibe: A lush, fungal gothic horror novel about a decaying English manor transplanted to the Mexican countryside, and the rot festering beneath its family's history.
novels.summary: Noemí travels to the remote, decaying mansion High Place to check on her newly married cousin, whose unsettling letters hint that something is deeply wrong with her new husband's family. As Noemí digs into the house's history of colonialism, eugenics, and rot, she uncovers a body-horror secret literally growing in the walls.
novels.warnings: Body horror, sexual assault (attempted), incest themes, colonial/eugenics themes, gore, drug use (non-consensual).

novels.title: The Haunting of Hill House
novels.author: Shirley Jackson (1959)
novels.vibe: The gothic haunted-house novel every other haunted-house novel is quietly arguing with, built on dread rather than gore.
novels.summary: Four seekers, including a scholar of the paranormal and the fragile, lonely Eleanor, take up residence in Hill House to study its reputed hauntings. The house's influence grows increasingly personal and psychological rather than overtly supernatural, tightening around Eleanor in particular as the group's grip on reality frays.
novels.warnings: Suicide (by hanging and by car collision), suicidal ideation, mental illness/psychosis, gaslighting, death of a parent (off-page).

short_works.title: The Fall of the House of Usher
short_works.author: Edgar Allan Poe (1839)
short_works.vibe: The gothic short story that defined the crumbling-mansion genre — a decaying house, a doomed family line, and a premature burial.
short_works.summary: A visitor arrives at the ancestral home of his old friend Roderick Usher, finding both the man and his house in advanced states of decay, seemingly bound to each other's decline. As Roderick's twin sister Madeline succumbs to a mysterious illness, the family's collapse and the house's collapse converge in a single catastrophic night.
short_works.warnings: Death, premature burial, mental illness/psychological horror, familial decline, implied incestuous undertones.

short_works.title: The Ruins of Contracoeur
short_works.author: Joyce Carol Oates (2006)
short_works.vibe: A YA-leaning gothic mystery about teenagers drawn into the ruins of an abandoned, legend-shrouded mansion on the edge of town.
short_works.summary: Teenager Rowan Hess and her friends explore the crumbling, long-abandoned Contracoeur estate on a dare, drawn in by local legends about the mansion's disappeared original owners. As they dig deeper into the ruins and the town's buried history, they uncover secrets the Contracoeur family — and the town itself — worked hard to forget.
short_works.warnings: Death, family tragedy, mild peril, themes of grief and disappearance.

short_works.title: The Judge's House
short_works.author: Bram Stoker (1891)
short_works.vibe: A classic haunted-house short from the author of Dracula — a student's isolated study retreat in a shunned old mansion goes very wrong.
short_works.summary: Seeking peace and quiet to study for exams, Malcolm Malcolmson rents a long-vacant, ill-reputed old house once owned by a cruel hanging judge, ignoring the locals' warnings. As strange occurrences mount around an unshakeable rat and a mysterious old chair, the house's grim history reasserts itself.
short_works.warnings: Death, hanging/execution themes, supernatural threat, disturbing imagery.
